answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through repeated, audited work: a task is assigned with a random cipher, peers verify the result, and a portion of payment stays locked until later checks pass. A reputation ledger links each verified contribution to a costly stake, so creating a fresh identity starts with no influence. An attacker must therefore fund many deposits and produce useful work that survives audits; abandoning exposed identities forfeits stake. Even a summit of coordinated fake agents faces that recurring cost, rather than gaining power by sheer headcount as the tide turns.
